The game is okay at best. I do want to give credit to the devs as is there is a love of detail in the kind of way the game is set up. However, the game lost me within a couple of hours as i expected a  soothing and cozy game, yet got hit in the face right away with a VERY in depth character customization menu before the actual game even began. For me, this was overwhelming and set the tone that glamour is more important than content ... sadly the Main menu does have a similar vibe with the very prominent ads for dlc that only seem to contain accesories. 

Right of the gate I got simply no idea what my character was supposed to be, why I went to that village and why the heck I was going to start a farm. In fact - you just get dropped of at some plot of land like "here is your farm, have fun" - right then you already have basic tools and stuff - which is nice - however the game doesn't lead you on. It kinda feels like i am expected to know right away how these farming sims work and imho that made me loose interest in the world itself pretty much immediately. The villagers seem fine i guess - tbh i didnt endure enough of this to actually form an opinion about the NPCs. 

Maybe the game has potential - but overall the "just getting thrown in" kinda thing, the overwhelming menus, number of npcs, the huge map from the get go and the cluttered UI didnt make for a soothing cozy game but a sensoric nightmare. I am so sorry, i really tried to like it but simply could comprehend all of it. When i wanna play something like this, i want a game that feels like a fuzzy blanket and hot chocolate - something easy to make me relax from my dayjob - and this simply wasn't it.

While the game isn't bad by any means, I would recommend against purchasing it due to how poorly the developers have been treated. It's up to you who you want to support, but it's good to be aware of where your money is going.

I really like the concept of this game and it seems like it'd be fun if it'd load properly. But spending 3+ minutes on one loading screen kills the gameplay immersion for me. So far I have clocked 8+ hours in the game but I can bet 1-3 hours was spent waiting for scenes to load, especially if I was traveling toward a dense part of the map. With some loading scenes, I had enough time to pick up a book and read a few pages, it's THAT bad. At least for me. The end for me was the game glitching on a load screen and the character doesn't seem to be playable after that, even with many reboots of the game. I can't find it in me to start a new character already. I'd rather just get a refund and never play it again.

I think this game needs a lot of work still. Some other things have come to light since I purchased it, and I kind of regret purchasing now. There's considerable lag, which I have been told is "Part of the game and is not scheduled to be fixed." as well as new bugs like suddenly not being able to make new characters because the choose birthday button does not work. There is no support via here or discord. I also dislike that there is no way to quickly skip dialogue. 

It is a fun game, but this feels like a beta version, not the full release.

I've put a lot of time over the years into the game on various profiles, but I think it's hard to leave a thumbs up review. I've enjoyed it, don't get me wrong, but I feel the current and latest edition of it is actually a bit gross. I find it hard to keep interest moving in past year 1, as I have 4 profiles now in the latest stages of Year 1 Winter.

On my last playthrough with my sister, there just seems to be so much extra stuff that just kinda gets in the way or feels like it's unnecessary when there could be a bit more hashed into what's already there. For example, There seem to be 3 extra town maps each with it's own story and romanceable character. Sounds great for new content, but the maps are given just tons of extra NPCs that you don't care about, which I feel they could hash out more in the already existing 3 maps that each have a playable farm. Seems to be a ton, but not much depth.

Things I like:
-We got magic stardew. Planting and watering feels so nice to just blast it away with a raincloud and call it good. Though the sprinkler supremacy is convenient and the auto-win alternative, just having that magic option feels like a fun alternative.
-Mounts! Though sometimes it's a bit inconvenient to be on a giant mount and take up a lot of space, it's nice to feel like you're an animal tamer riding on an animal in addition to having a leashed pet to follow with you.
-Skill tree is lengthy and you can eventually max them out. I like being able to max out so that's always been fun.
-High stat ceilings. Food gives permanent stats with diminishing values which is nice, but sometimes it feels too much when there are just SOOO many foods and golden versions of food, feels just unnecessary to be honest.
-Co-op is kinda a must. It's co-op. Not much else to say about it.

Things that could be better:
-Me and my sister are on the last boss of the mines, but it seems we have separate progress in fighting it- like we each have our own boss to fight that the other doesn't see. Very lame especially since in the trailer for the game they look to be cooperatively fighting together
-Too much bloat. Other reviews say it. It's real. Sometimes the maps are just super cluttered with extra garbage you can break for 1 coin or an apple core. Very ugly to be honest.
-Farming actually starts to feel unnecessary to keep up with. There are incentives to hoarding in this game, so I tend to just hold onto select crops but never planting anything different. Eventually just don't even take care of crops.

I'll say I got a lot of play out of it, and I still plan to play more with my sister, but I'd say there are other farming sims that I think are better hashed out.

Sun Haven is a very fun gameplay experience. I've always had a soft spot for fully-selectable skill-tree growth systems and putting one in a Stardew-alike activates my satisfaction in a way other games in this genre just DON'T. Native multiplayer allowing you to capitalize on this by specializing in-contrast to those you play with and gives you a very fun soft class system with tangible bonuses outside of just declaring yourself The Mines Guy, or The Farmer, or The Animal Caretaker. It's something I wish more farm-sim games did, at least in a more directly-granular fashion like this.

That said, I also bought this game before learning of the developer's extremely sketchy behavior in regards to compensating and crediting its artists while still churning out scads of paid-cosmetic DLC the entire time (just below $200 USD for a $30 game at the time of writing) - if I HAD known beforehand, I wouldn't have bought this, and thus it's become a very "Can't un-nugget the chicken" situation for me personally. Kind of my fault for not paying attention to this sort of thing, but so often you don't quite expect the need to look up developer allegations when they aren't immediately apparent. So it goes.

This is a game I very much adore playing and praise what does correctly, but cannot ethically recommend to anyone who hasn't bought it due to actions of its developer management. Learn from those of us who made the mistake first: do not monetarily support a studio like this.

(EDIT: I wrote this review before learning about the disappointing issues with the developer. Sun Haven is NOT a game worth 207$ for all its features, Devs are you *insane*? Like legitimately, seriously, I would love to know. The 37$ base game price tag is *already* pushing it for the kind of game it is.

1) The "Main story" is locked behind seasonal items, meaning if you get to that point in the story and you've just past that season then guess what? Gotta wait a whole in game year to grow the produce/get the seasonal item to progress. This is unnecessary padding.

2) Game loop is shallow, as is the character developments and relationships. You can romance certain characters, sure, but unlike Stardew you're not participating in their life, you're just watching it unfold for you once you hit the story beats.

3) There's an insane amount of backtracking. You'll make progress, scroll your screen over once and then OOP GOTTA GO BACK TO FIRST MAIN TOWN TM TO GO SPEAK TO SPECIFIC NPC SO YOU CAN *maybe* FINALLY GET TO THE NEXT ZONE. Like, I remember having to put the game down after I had collected not a small amount of ressources for a main quest to progress, only to have to go back and suddenly get a crap load of MORE ressources... just because I guess. Also why the F*&^ do you block entire pathways to your farm based on the season for a quest you have to do over and over again? Stop that, its annoying.

4) Ethical and Moral considerations; I cannot in good conscience recommend this developper studio due to their working practices and business practices.

5) Catgirl is cringe and annoying to talk to but this game INSISTS that I must interacts with her because they think "Dumb girl that speaks in third person" is good characterization.

6) They seem to want you to feel like "The Chosen One" without any of "The Chosen One Privileges.

Note: This review isn't about the developers - I do agree that their documented actions towards their workers have been really horrendous. I got this game before Pixel Sprout Studios did that stuff, when this was recommended by some users in a Discord community I was in. I caved in, and occasionally played with said users.

To say it short and sweet, this is not my cup of tea, even though I should enjoy this genre's games. The thing that didn't sit with me was the extensive amount of features, funnily enough: As an example, while Stardew Valley can be monotonous in many areas, it's quite a simple game in its core features. You attend your crops and animals, maybe gather resources like wood, fight enemies in the caves, or do tasks revolving around the NPCs. When you play enough, you get access to some more stuff, some which can be complex. With Sun Haven, I felt there were a lot of small things to do in the beginning which overwhelmed me.

I had the itch to return to this game. I am glad (in a future sense that) I didn't fulfill on it: I feel sorry for those who enjoyed this game, only to get crushed emotionally due to what the developers did.

The game is so much fun, but I haven't played in a year since learning about how the developers treat the people working on the game. Please do some research on the situation before you buy any game from Pixel Sprout Studios. It's really sad. I've basically been in mourning.
